mainTopic: Why vowed items (a דבר שיש לו מתירין) are not cancelled among permitted growths while תרומה is, and רבי יוחנן's ruling on tithed onions that were planted
overview: This amud continues the discussion of the view that permitted growths from the ground can cancel out a forbidden seed. First the גמרא finishes an answer about tithes: the duty to tithe starts when the grain is piled up, not in the ground. רמי בר חמא then challenges the view from a משנה about vows (קונם), where even growths of growths can stay forbidden. רבי אבא answers that vows are a דבר שיש לו מתירין, because a חכם can release them, and such an item is not cancelled by a majority. The גמרא pushes back from תרומה, which can also be released yet is cancelled in a hundred. It tries two case answers: תרומה already in the כהן's hand, and a ישראל who inherited it from a כהן grandfather. The end of the משנה knocks down both. Finally the גמרא says that only vows carry a מצוה to be released, because of רבי נתן's teaching, and תרומה does not. The amud then returns to רבי יוחנן's ruling that tithed onions which were planted are tithed on the whole crop. רב חסדא challenges it, and רבה begins to answer with a משנה about onions that sprouted in the rain, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The tithe duty comes from piling the grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question about tithes: the duty to tithe is triggered by piling the produce, not by the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: with tithe, it is the piling of the produce that creates the obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer to a question it raised just before this point. The question was about tithes. The answer is that the tithe obligation starts when the grain is piled up, not when it grows from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the obligation to separate מעשר only starts at the piling stage (דיגון), the ground has nothing to cancel. So tithes do not disprove the idea that the ground can cancel a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe, the tenth of the produce that must be separated
Piling or smoothing the grain into a heap. This is the stage that makes produce obligated in tithes

phrases.english: They say: tithe —
it is the piling that causes it (the obligation).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מַעֲשֵׂר, דִּיגּוּן הוּא דְּקָא גָרֵים לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question about tithes that was raised on the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the source of the obligation: it comes from piling, not from the ground
steps.terutzMaskana: The tithe obligation begins at דיגון, so tithes are no proof against the ground cancelling a prohibition.

steps.title: Challenge from the vow case where growths stay forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges the idea that permitted growths cancel a forbidden seed. He uses a משנה about קונם vows, where even growths of growths stay forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: If someone says "These fruits are קונם on me," or "on my mouth," or "to my mouth," then their replacements and their growths are forbidden. If he says "that I eat" or "that I taste," then replacements and growths are permitted when the seed rots away in the ground. But when the seed does not rot away, even growths of growths are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא quotes a משנה about vows to attack the view that the ground cancels a prohibition. In that משנה, some growths of forbidden produce stay forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If permitted growth from the soil cancelled the forbidden seed, the growths of a vowed fruit should become permitted. Instead the משנה says that when the seed stays in the plant, even growths of growths are forbidden. That suggests the ground does not cancel the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow that forbids an item, like declaring it a קרבן
Their replacements: items received in exchange for them
Their growths: what grows from planting them
A plant whose seed rots away in the ground after planting

steps.confusionAlert: "שאני אוכל" does not mean the person is allowed to eat. He means "[these are קונם] so that I will not eat them." This vow forbids his act of eating, so it is weaker than a vow on the fruit itself.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama raised an objection:
"These fruits are konam upon me,"
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found earlier in this פרק.

phrases.english: "they are konam upon my mouth,"
"they are konam to my mouth" —
he is forbidden in their replacements and in their growths.
"that I eat," or "that I taste" —
he is permitted in their replacements and their growths
in an item whose seed ceases (rots away),
but in an item whose seed does not cease —
even growths of growths are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tithe question is settled, a new challenge is brought against the view that the ground cancels a prohibition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that permitted growths cancel a forbidden seed planted in the ground
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קונם משנה says growths of growths stay forbidden when the seed does not rot. So the permitted growth from the soil does not cancel the forbidden seed.

steps.title: Vows are different because they can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that vowed items are a special case. The vow can be released by a חכם, so the item counts as a דבר שיש לו מתירין, which is never cancelled by a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: Vows are different. Since the person can ask a חכם to cancel them if he wants, they are like an item that has a way to become permitted, and such an item is not cancelled by a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא defends the earlier view. He explains that the vow case is an exception and does not disprove the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a דבר שיש לו מתירין (something that can become permitted another way) is not cancelled by a majority. Why wait for cancellation when you can simply permit it? Since a vow can be released through התרה, the growths stay forbidden. The general rule about the ground cancelling still holds elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different: introduces a special case
Asks a חכם to release a vow (שאלה על נדר)
An item that can become permitted in another way, so it is not cancelled in a mixture

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a דבר שיש לו מתירין is not cancelled in a mixture is a major principle across the laws of mixtures (תערובות).

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Konamot (vowed items) are different,
since, if he wants, he can ask (for release) on them —
phrases.notes: He means going to a חכם to have the vow cancelled.

phrases.aramaic: הָווּ לְהוּ כְּדָבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: they are like an item that has a way to become permitted,
and it is not cancelled by a majority.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: vows are a דבר שיש לו מתירין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קונם משנה seemed to show that the ground never cancels a prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vows are an exception because they can be released, so they are not cancelled by a majority. The general rule is not disproved.

steps.title: Challenge from תרומה that is cancelled in a hundred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא. תרומה can also be released by asking a חכם, yet a משנה shows it is cancelled in a hundred parts of חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at תרומה: if he wants, he can ask for release on it, and yet it is cancelled in a majority. As we learned: a סאה of impure תרומה that fell into less than a hundred סאה of חולין must be left to rot. That means if it fell into a hundred, it is cancelled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אבא's reasoning with a case that seems to work the same way. That case is תרומה, which also can be cancelled by a חכם but still gets cancelled in a mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said that anything that can be released by asking a חכם is a דבר שיש לו מתירין and is not cancelled. A person can also ask to undo his separation of תרומה. Yet the משנה implies that one part in a hundred is cancelled. So the reasoning seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
It must be left to rot (it cannot be used)
Literally "it goes up": it is cancelled in the mixture

phrases.english: But there is terumah,
where, if he wants, he can ask (for release) on it,
and yet it is cancelled in a majority.
As we learned in a mishnah:
A se'a of impure terumah
that fell into less than a hundred (se'a) of non-holy produce —
must be left to rot.
So into a hundred, it is cancelled!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי תְּרוּמָה, דְּאִי בָּעֵי מִיתְּשִׁיל עֲלַהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's principle that anything which can be released by a חכם is not cancelled by a majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה can also be released by a חכם, yet the משנה implies it is cancelled in a hundred.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of תרומה already given to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תרומה משנה speaks about תרומה already in the כהן's hand. Once it is there, the owner can no longer ask to cancel it, so it is not a דבר שיש לו מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: we are dealing with תרומה that is in the hand of a כהן, which he can no longer ask to release.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבא by narrowing the תרומה משנה to a case where release is no longer possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the תרומה reaches the כהן, the owner can no longer undo it. With no way to permit it, it is an ordinary prohibited item, so it can be cancelled in a hundred. רבי אבא's principle stands: while release is possible, there is no cancellation.

keyTerms.meaning: In the possession of a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: This answer does not last. Step 6 challenges it, step 8 knocks down the follow-up answer, and step 9 replaces both with a new reason.

phrases.english: They say:
We are dealing with terumah in the hand of a kohen,
which he cannot ask (for release) on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תרומה challenge and defends רבי אבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a situation where release is no longer possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה seemed to be releasable and yet cancelled, which would contradict רבי אבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of תרומה in the כהן's hand, which cannot be released, so it is cancelled like any ordinary prohibition.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows the תרומה is still with its owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 5. The end of the תרומה משנה says the mixture should be sold to a כהן, which suggests the תרומה never reached a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of that משנה: if the mixture was pure, it should be sold to a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 5, that the משנה is about תרומה already in the כהן's hand. It points to the end of that same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה says a pure mixture must be sold to a כהן. A כהן who already owned the תרומה would simply eat it and would not need to sell it to anyone. So the משנה must be about an owner who still holds the תרומה, and that owner could still ask a חכם to cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you just said is true)
The latter clause or end part of a משנה

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
If it was pure, it should be sold to a כהן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setting proposed in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה speaks of תרומה already in the כהן's hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Selling the mixture to a כהן only makes sense if a non-כהן owner still holds the תרומה, and such an owner can still ask a חכם to cancel it.

steps.title: A non-כהן who inherited the תרומה from his mother's father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the case. The owner is a ישראל who inherited the תרומה from his maternal grandfather, who was a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are dealing with a ישראל who inherited it from his mother's father, who was a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the idea by changing the case. The owner is a regular ישראל who inherited the תרומה from his grandfather, a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This heir really owns the תרומה, so it makes sense for him to sell it to a כהן. But he is not the one who set it aside as תרומה, so he cannot ask a חכם to cancel it. That means it is still not a דבר שיש לו מתירין.

phrases.english: Rather, with a ישראל to whom it fell
phrases.notes: "Fell to him" is the גמרא's usual way of saying he inherited it.

phrases.english: from the house of his mother's father, a כהן, we are dealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לוֹ מִבֵּית אֲבִי אִמּוֹ כֹּהֵן עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling to a כהן proves an owner who could ask to cancel the תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner is an heir. He owns the תרומה but cannot ask to cancel it, because he did not set it aside.

steps.title: Why would the heir lose the value of his own סאה?
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says the mixture is sold to a כהן except for the value of the fallen סאה. That does not fit an heir who owns that סאה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the משנה teaches: it is sold to a כהן, except for the value of that סאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the heir case from step 7, using another detail in the same end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the seller does not get paid for the סאה of תרומה, because it belongs to the כהן. If the seller inherited that תרומה, it is his own property, so he should be paid for it too. So the heir case does not fit the משנה.

phrases.english: But doesn't the latter clause teach:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: תִּימָּכֵר לְכֹהֵן חוּץ מִדְּמֵי אוֹתָהּ סְאָה?
phrases.english: It is sold to a כהן except for the value of that סאה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the heir case from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner is a ישראל heir of a כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An heir owns the תרומה, so there is no reason to subtract its value. The subtraction shows the תרומה belongs to someone else, a כהן.

steps.title: Only vows carry a מצוה to be released
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier answers and gives a new distinction. There is a מצוה to release vows, because of רבי נתן's teaching, but there is no such מצוה for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: with vows, it makes sense. There is a מצוה to ask a חכם to release them, because of רבי נתן. רבי נתן said: whoever makes a vow is like someone who built a private altar, and whoever keeps the vow is like someone burning an offering on it. But with תרומה, what מצוה is there to ask to release it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the case answers from steps 5 and 7. It answers the תרומה challenge against רבי אבא (step 4) in a brand-new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to ask a חכם is not enough to make something a דבר שיש לו מתירין. Vows count because there is actually a מצוה to have them released, since vowing is compared to building a forbidden private altar. תרומה has no such מצוה, so it is treated as an ordinary forbidden item and gets cancelled in a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made forbidden by a vow
To ask a חכם to release
A private altar outside the בית המקדש (forbidden)

steps.whatToRemember: A דבר שיש לו מתירין is not just anything that could be released. It is something that should be released. Vows have a מצוה to be released, and תרומה does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the earlier answers are still standing. The words "אלא אימא" mean the גמרא is dropping them and switching to a new reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a vowed item is never cancelled in a majority, while תרומה is cancelled in a hundred parts.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Granted with vows, there is a מצוה to request release from them,
because of רבי נתן.
For רבי נתן said:
Anyone who vows is as if he built a private altar,
and one who keeps it is as if he burns an offering on it.
With תרומה, what מצוה is there to request release from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 knocks out the case answers, gives a new answer to the question from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction based on the presence of a מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything a חכם can release counts as a דבר שיש לו מתירין, so תרומה should count too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only items with a מצוה to be released, like vows, count. תרומה does not, so it is cancelled in a majority.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: tithed onions that were planted are tithed on the whole crop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's statement itself. A ליטרא of onions that was tithed and then planted must be tithed on the entire crop. רבה taught this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. רבי יוחנן said: a ליטרא of onions that someone tithed and then planted is tithed on the whole crop. רבה sat and taught this ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן's statement, which was quoted earlier, so it can discuss it on its own. It also tells us רבה taught it, setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the original ליטרא was already tithed, the whole harvest, including the part that matches the original amount, must be tithed again. This fits step 1: the tithing duty starts when the produce is piled up, and the new crop is a brand-new harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself (a return to a statement quoted earlier)
That he fixed it (tithed it so it may be eaten)

phrases.english: The matter itself: רבי יוחנן said:
A ליטרא of onions that he tithed and planted
is tithed according to all of it.
רבה sat and stated this ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the vow and תרומה discussion and returns to רבי יוחנן's original statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Onions that were tithed and then planted must be tithed on the entire new crop.

steps.title: רב חסדא: where did the already-tithed part go?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the ruling. The original ליטרא was already permitted, so why should it be tithed again?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Who listens to you and to your teacher רבי יוחנן? The permitted part of the onions, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא strongly challenges the ruling רבה just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original ליטרא was already tithed and permitted. So רב חסדא argues that at least that amount should be taken off the new crop, and only the extra growth should need tithing.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן צָאֵית לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ!
phrases.english: Who listens to you and to רבי יוחנן your teacher!
The permitted part in them, where did it go?
phrases.notes: He means the original ליטרא, which was already tithed before it was planted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן צָאֵית לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling stated in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the whole crop must be tithed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The original amount was already permitted, so it should not need tithing again.

steps.title: רבה brings a matching משנה about onions that sprouted in the rain
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers by pointing to a משנה with a similar rule, about onions that sprouted after rain fell on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't we learn a similar case in a משנה: onions that rain fell on and they sprouted...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts defending רבי יוחנן by quoting a משנה with a matching rule. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is setting up a proof. In the משנה, onions that sprouted get treated by the status of the new growth, and the original permitted part is not set aside. That would support treating the whole new crop as fresh.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי לָא תְּנַן דִּכְווֹתַהּ:
phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't we learn a matching case:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שביעית, and the quote continues past this point.

phrases.english: Onions on which rain fell and they sprouted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה answers רב חסדא's challenge with support from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the whole new crop is tithed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית about onions that sprouted after rain.
